guide.headline: At the 10mg cap, rosin wins: HighXotic TenTens, Fly North and Glenn's are the gummies people say actually hit
guide.lede: The most consistent advice in these threads is to buy rosin, not distillate. HighXotic TenTen singles, Fly North Space Tokens and Glenn's rosin gummies are the ones people say really work at 10mg, at roughly $1.20–3.50 per 10mg, and Glenn's and Fly North are the cheapest. If you need 30mg or more, capsules and drops cost far less per mg. Drinks taste good but cost a lot for the dose, and the rosin cans (Astrolab, Sheesh, Snap Back) are the ones people say they can feel.

trends.title: Rosin and full-spectrum are replacing distillate
trends.detail: In nearly every thread, people say live or hash rosin gummies (HighXotic, Fly North, Glenn's) and rosin capsules hit harder or feel 'more complete' than distillate. One person says they need 20mg of rosin versus 40mg of distillate. The same split shows up in drinks: Sheesh, Astrolab and Snap Back rosin cans are preferred over nano and distillate sodas. A vocal minority says 10mg is 10mg and calls the difference placebo.
trends.means: If 10mg distillate does nothing for you, try a rosin gummy before you double the dose.

trends.title: Gummies are moving to big packs
trends.detail: Fly North's Space Rocks put 20 x 10mg of live rosin on shelves at close to the 10-pack price (about $24.90). Glenn's has a 200s pack ($34.95 for 20), and Pearls sells 25-packs. Commenters citing OCS September 2026 data say producers replaced single-pack listings with 10-packs, so buyers who want one or two gummies are being squeezed out.
trends.means: Per-mg prices are falling, but singles are harder to find, and one buyer says big packs led them to take more than they meant to.

trends.title: More minor-cannabinoid ratio gummies and drinks
trends.detail: Recent launches include HighXotic TenTen Morning Dew (50mg CBG + 10mg THC) and Stillwater (5:1 CBC), No Future CBG/CBD Cluster Bomb 10-packs, and a Pearls CBC 25-pack. Mollo seltzers now reportedly include 20mg CBG. People use CBG and CBC for a daytime lift without sedation, and CBN for sleep. A few find CBG's buzz 'weird' or report a crash afterward.
trends.means: For a clear daytime high, look for CBG or CBC ratios. CBN versions are meant for bed.

trends.title: DIY drinks with water-soluble drops
trends.detail: Many people have stopped buying $6–9 cans and add MOD drops, Spark rosin drops or Emprise mixes to their own drinks or a SodaStream. MOD's 1000mg pack makes about a hundred 10mg drinks for about $50–60. The trade-off is taste: the drops are bitter, so people hide them in coffee, citrus or chocolate milk.
trends.means: If you like drinks but not the prices, drops cost roughly a tenth as much per 10mg.

trends.title: Cannabis drinks are shrinking on shelves
trends.detail: Versus pulled Neon Rush Bolt from OCS wholesale entirely, and a Vacay flavour was delisted. PEI Cannabis stopped carrying Astrolab rosin sodas, and Astrolab's parent, Simply Solventless, is reported to be in CCAA proceedings. One retailer says drinks are only about 2.3% of their sales and the margins are thin.
trends.means: If you have a favourite can, especially Astrolab, expect gaps in supply.

trends.title: Low- and zero-sugar drinks
trends.detail: Bubble Kush promised a 3g-sugar 'Natural' line for late July 2026, and a Natural Blueberry Pomegranate ($7.95) is now in the OCS catalog. M*ry Jones Zero Sugar sodas and Mollo's zero-sugar seltzers get good reviews. Full-sugar cans like Palmetto (37g), Sweet Tooth (39g) and XMG Cream Soda (43g) keep drawing complaints.
trends.means: There are now decent options if sugar is the reason you've avoided cans, though some people dislike the sweeteners.

trends.title: HighXotic packaging problems
trends.detail: Budtenders report TenTen bags with bad or diagonal seals, with gummies melting, leaking or 'sweating' out. One store sent back about 15. The brand's AI-generated box art also caused a backlash, with some shops saying they'd stop carrying it. HighXotic reportedly said its next packaging will be drawn by two artists.
trends.means: Check that the bag is sealed and dry before you leave the store, and keep TenTens in the fridge.

trends.title: Capsules and tablets as the way past the cap
trends.detail: Sugar-free ingestibles come in 300–1000mg packs, so Moonrocks 100-packs, Rosin Heads drops, Simply Bare softgels and oils are the usual advice for anyone who needs 30mg or more. Aspire added an RSO Reserve tablet, but some buyers find it weaker, and recent Live Rosin Reserve batches have stopped printing the strain. Aspire's lozenges were discontinued.
trends.means: High-tolerance buyers save the most by skipping gummies, but expect potency to vary from one product line to the next.

trends.title: Old drink cans re-stickered, and stamps on the mouthpiece
trends.detail: A Sheesh founder explained that unsold 2024 lots can be retested and re-stickered with a new packaged date, and that flavour fades as can liners absorb it. Separately, people keep complaining that the excise stamp glue sits right where you drink.
trends.means: Peel back the sticker to see the original packaged date, and wipe the rim before you drink.

tips.title: Smoking tolerance doesn't carry over
tips.body: Heavy smokers are routinely surprised in both directions: some feel nothing at 100mg, others get knocked over by 10mg. Start with half a gummy, especially a HighXotic TenTen or Fly North rosin. Give it at least an hour, or longer, before taking more.

tips.title: Eat some fat with it, but Moonrocks may be the exception
tips.body: Most people say gummies, oils and RSO work better with peanut butter, ice cream, yogurt or chai. One user insists Aspire Moonrocks are water-soluble and hit fastest on an empty stomach with water (45–60 min, versus 2h+ after food).

tips.title: Over 30mg, buy capsules or drops instead
tips.body: 10mg gummies run about $1.20–3.50 per 10mg. Moonrocks 100-packs, MOD drops and oils work out to about $0.50–0.60 per 10mg, and Rosin Heads drops or Simply Bare softgels are the full-spectrum middle ground.

tips.title: Check the package before you buy
tips.body: Look for 'rosin' versus 'distillate' on the label. Check the packaged date, and peek under drink stickers. Make sure TenTen bags are sealed and dry. Pearls go rock-hard after about a week, so buy what you'll eat.

tips.title: Cut for small doses
tips.body: Use a knife on a cutting board. Olli sticks don't break evenly, and people cut Pearls into halves or thirds. Keeping TenTens in the fridge firms them up and makes them easier to cut.

tips.title: Shop around with Hibuddy
tips.body: Hibuddy.ca shows which nearby stores have a product in stock and at what price. Commenters say OCS charges full suggested retail, while private stores often discount, with Glenn's rosin as low as $1.40–1.50 and No Future 10-packs around $18.

glossary.definition: Refined THC oil with the plant's other compounds stripped out. It's cheap and consistent, but often described as 'flat' or one-dimensional in edibles.
Solventless extract pressed with heat from fresh-frozen plant or ice-water hash. Rosin gummies are what most people say actually hit at 10mg.
Solvent-extracted concentrate. It keeps more of the plant than distillate, but fans rank it below rosin. Woody Nelson uses cured resin.
Extract that keeps minor cannabinoids and terpenes. People say it feels fuller or more body-centred than distillate, and some need less of it.
Rick Simpson Oil, a thick, potent full-plant oil sold in syringes (e.g. Ellevia). A tiny drop can be 50mg or more, and onset can take hours.
A non-intoxicating cannabinoid people describe as uplifting or a 'happy pill'. It's paired with THC for daytime gummies like Morning Dew and Pearls 3:1.
A cannabinoid mostly marketed for sleep (Pearls Lemon Dream, Blackberry Lemonade). Some people wake up groggy after it.
Minor cannabinoids showing up in ratio gummies. CBC is described as social and euphoric. THCV is pitched as a munchie-blocker, though not everyone finds it works.
THC processed to mix with water (MOD drops, Shotz, Emprise, Aspire Rapid Sense). People say it starts in about 15–30 minutes and often wears off sooner.
Sugar-free capsules, tablets, drops and oils. They fall under extract rules, so one package can hold far more than 10mg of THC, which is how people get around the gummy cap.

faq.q: Will a 10mg legal gummy actually do anything?
faq.a: It depends heavily on the product and on you. Distillate 10mg often feels like little to regular smokers, while rosin gummies like HighXotic TenTen, Fly North Space Tokens and Glenn's rosin are repeatedly described as hitting well above their weight. Some heavy users still need 30mg or more, and a few feel almost nothing from any edible.

faq.q: Is live rosin really stronger than distillate, or is it hype?
faq.a: Most commenters say rosin feels stronger and more complete. One says they need 20mg of rosin versus 40mg of distillate, and in a head-to-head Fly North beat Sourz Fully Blasted easily. A vocal minority says 10mg is 10mg and the difference is placebo, and one person has questioned whether 'live rosin' labels listing only 'cannabis extract' are verifiable.

faq.q: How long until it kicks in, and how long does it last?
faq.a: Regular gummies range from about 45 minutes to 3+ hours depending on food and the person, then run for hours. TenTen fans report being 'baked for hours'. Drinks and nano products start in about 10–30 minutes and may wear off sooner. RSO can take 4–6+ hours. Don't redose early.

faq.q: What's the cheapest way to get more than 10mg legally?
faq.a: Capsules, tablets, drops and oils: Aspire Moonrocks at about $60 for 100 x 10mg, MOD drops at about $50–60 per 1000mg, and 30:0 oils at about $30–40 for roughly 900mg. Among gummies, Fly North's Space Rocks 20-pack (about $1.18 per 10mg) and Glenn's rosin singles (about $1.50–1.95) are the cheapest rosin.

faq.q: Which edibles won't make me sleepy?
faq.a: CBG and CBC ratio gummies come up most often: HighXotic Morning Dew and Stillwater, Pearls Blue Razzleberry, SOURZ Strawberry Watermelon 4:1 and Wyld ratios. Expect some comedown either way, since Stillwater gave one user a hard crash. Avoid anything with CBN, and indica rosin like Fly North Platinum Blueberry, during the day.

faq.q: Are cannabis drinks worth the money?
faq.a: Mostly for the taste. At $6–11 a can, many call them a novelty, and distillate drinks are often described as barely noticeable. The rosin cans (Astrolab, Sheesh, Snap Back) are the ones people say they feel. For value, people add drops to their own drinks.

faq.q: Will CBD, CBG or CBN gummies get me high?
faq.a: No. No Future CBD and CBG Bombs, Pearls CBN Lemon Dream and similar products give, at most, calm, focus or sleep support. Several first-timers expecting a buzz were disappointed. CBG seems to shine as an add-on to THC.

faq.q: What should I take for sleep?
faq.a: People who want THC use Fly North Platinum Blueberry ('sleep like a baby') or Pearls Blackberry Lemonade and Strawberry Melon (THC plus CBN). THC-free options are Pearls CBN Lemon Dream and Monjour CBN gummies. TenTens are flagged as too sugary for bedtime, and CBN leaves some people groggy.

start.summary: Take 2.5–5 mg of THC (a quarter to half of a standard 10 mg gummy, or part of a can), set a timer, and wait a full two hours before you even think about more. People say it can take that long to kick in, and once it's eaten you can't take it back.
start.first_time: If you're new or coming back after a long break, start with 2.5–5 mg of THC. That's a quarter or half of a 10 mg gummy, or roughly half of a 10 mg drink. People in the threads say 10 mg is the most you should take the first time, and some find even that intense.
start.wait: Wait at least 2 hours before taking more. Many people say to save any increase for another day. People report edibles taking anywhere from 30 minutes to over 2 hours to kick in, and the classic green-out story is taking a second dose because "it isn't working," then feeling both doses at once.

timeline.onset: 30 minutes to 2+ hours; drinks and "rapid" products often sooner
timeline.lasts: 6–12 hours, sometimes a groggy next morning

steps.title: Pick a free evening at home
steps.body: Plan to be somewhere comfortable with nowhere to be for the rest of the day and no driving until the next day. Ideally have someone with you who isn't taking anything. People stress the setting and having no responsibilities, and Canada's Lower-Risk Cannabis Use Guidelines say not to drive for at least 6 hours after using, longer if you still feel it.

steps.title: Read the label before you open it
steps.body: Check the mg of THC per piece, not just the total for the pack. Stick to legal OCS or licensed-store products. Several bad nights in the threads came from a corner-store gummy, a homemade edible or a THC-P product that was far stronger than the person thought.

steps.title: Take 2.5–5 mg with a light meal
steps.body: Cut a 10 mg gummy into quarters or halves (the THC is spread all through it, so it won't "fall out"), or pour half a can of a drink. Several people suggest taking it with ordinary food rather than on a totally empty or very full stomach.

steps.title: Set a timer for 2 hours and leave the rest alone
steps.body: Put on a movie or cook dinner, and don't judge the dose for at least 2 hours. A timer stops you from losing track and "topping up" early.

steps.title: If you add more, add a little
steps.body: If you feel nothing after 2–3 hours, people suggest another 2.5–5 mg at most, then waiting again. Many prefer to stop for the night and try a slightly bigger dose another day, since a late extra dose can stretch the high into the next morning.

steps.title: Don't stack alcohol or a joint on top
steps.body: For the first few times, keep it to the edible only. People report that alcohol both hides the high and makes it easier to overdo, and that smoking on top of an edible is how a nice evening turns into a green-out.

start.with_tolerance: People in the threads keep saying your smoking tolerance doesn't carry over to edibles. Heavy flower smokers (2–4 g a day) report that 10–20 mg of a rosin gummy flattened them, while others need 50 mg or more. Start with half to one 10 mg piece, wait the full 2 hours, and go up from there on another day.

first_picks.why: Low THC per piece; people call them a mild, functional buzz that's "perfect for low tolerance users."
Dosed drop by drop (0.5 mg drops are mentioned), so you can build up in very small steps in any drink.
Low-dose THC balanced with CBD and CBN; people describe the mix as relaxing rather than racy.

mistakes.title: Taking a second dose because the first "isn't working"
mistakes.body: This is the most common story: no effect after an hour, so another piece, then another, until everything kicks in together. People describe throwing up and riding it out all day.

mistakes.title: Eating a whole high-dose piece without checking the mg
mistakes.body: First-timers who ate a full 50 mg or 100 mg piece describe panic, a racing heart, a trip to the ER and feeling off the next day. Often a friend or cashier had told them it was a "normal dose."

mistakes.title: Assuming flower tolerance means edible tolerance
mistakes.body: Regular smokers report being caught off guard, especially by rosin gummies. One greened out on 40 mg, another on 100 mg on a bus, and a 2–4 g-a-day smoker was "blown away" by 20 mg.

mistakes.title: Mixing with alcohol and more smoking
mistakes.body: Edibles taken after drinks or on top of bong hits show up again and again in the worst nights, including someone who was pushed into it by hosts.

mistakes.title: Unknown or unusual products
mistakes.body: THC-P and unregulated gummies hit much harder and last far longer than people expected, sometimes for days. Slow digestion (for example on a GLP-1 medication) also made one person's edible come on late and last longer.

too_much: It passes. People who've been there say you'll come through it, even when it doesn't feel that way. Remind yourself the feeling is temporary.
Get somewhere safe to sit or lie down, and don't drive or go anywhere.
Slow your breathing (long, slow inhales and exhales) and let the anxious feeling be there instead of fighting it. People say that helps it ease.
Have some water and a snack, put on a familiar movie or music, or talk to a friend to take your mind off it.
Some people say CBD (or chewing a black peppercorn) takes the edge off for them. That's what people report, not a proven fix.

If you have chest pain, trouble breathing or you're worried, call Health Connect Ontario at 811 or 911. General advice: you can't take the edible back, so getting help is better than waiting it out alone.

quotes.text: Start with 5mg, you can always take more but you cant put the genie back in the bottle if you take too much.
Use timers, you really don't want to over do it.
Smoking tolerance isn't 1:1 with edible tolerance
Half a can is a good first attempt.

The good thing is you will always survive the bad thing is sometimes it doesn’t feel like you will.

start.evidence_note: Many people across Ontario and general threads agree on the method: 2.5–5 mg to start, wait hours, don't redose early, and smoking tolerance doesn't carry over. The 811/911 and no-driving points come from general harm-reduction guidance.
